decisions.reason: The polymer concrete housing has a page of its own and fits the firm's core drainage families, so its value is still uncertain but promising and carrying it costs little.
The floor-level shower system matches the firm's strategic move toward accessible low-profile solutions, so keeping the option open is cheap while demand develops.
As the flagship of its design direction, it has high strategic option value and no evidence that this value will go unrealized.
The sloped shower element supports integrated floor-level shower systems; its uncertainty is unresolved and its carrying cost is modest because it shares components with existing lines.
The backflow-protected basement drain was specifically developed and promoted, and it addresses a real protection need, so it is worth continuing while market results come in.
The air-admittance valve is peripheral and only mentioned on the website, but it is a low-cost complementary item that rounds out the drainage range, so dropping it now is premature.
